message.content:
Below is a concise list of the **long‑weekend periods** that Canadians enjoyed in 2023.  
A “long weekend” is defined as a stretch of **three or more consecutive days off** that includes a statutory holiday (or an observed holiday when the statutory holiday falls on a weekend).

| Long‑Weekend Period | Holiday(s) Involved | Notes |
|---------------------|---------------------|-------|
| **Dec 31 2022 – Jan 2 2023** | New Year’s Day (observed Jan 2) | New Year’s Day fell on Sunday Jan 1, so the holiday was observed on Monday Jan 2. The weekend of Dec 31 – Jan 1 plus the observed day gives a 4‑day break. |
| **May 20 – 22 2023** | Victoria Day | Victoria Day is always on the Monday preceding May 25. In 2023 it was Monday May 22, giving a 3‑day weekend (Sat 20–Mon 22). |
| **July 1 – 3 2023** | Canada Day (observed July 3) | Canada Day fell on Saturday July 1, so the holiday was observed on Monday July 3. The weekend of July 1–2 plus the observed day gives a 3‑day break. |
| **Sep 2 – 4 2023** | Labour Day | Labour Day is the first Monday in September. In 2023 it was Monday Sep 4, giving a 3‑day weekend (Sat 2–Mon 4). |
| **Oct 7 – 9 2023** | Thanksgiving | Thanksgiving is the second Monday in October. In 2023 it was Monday Oct 9, giving a 3‑day weekend (Sat 7–Mon 9). |
| **Nov 11 – 13 2023** | Remembrance Day (observed Nov 13) | Remembrance Day fell on Saturday Nov 11, so the holiday was observed on Monday Nov 13. The weekend of Nov 11–12 plus the observed day gives a 3‑day break. |
| **Dec 23 – 26 2023** | Christmas (Mon 25) & Boxing Day (Tue 26) | Christmas fell on Monday Dec 25 and Boxing Day on Tuesday Dec 26. Combined with the preceding weekend (Sat 23–Sun 24) this created a 4‑day holiday stretch. |

---

### Provincial Variations (Optional)

Some provinces observe additional statutory holidays that also create long weekends. If your app needs province‑specific data, here are the most common ones for 2023:

| Province | Holiday | Date | Long‑Weekend Result |
|----------|---------|------|---------------------|
| Ontario | Family Day | Feb 20 | Feb 18–20 |
| British Columbia | Family Day | Feb 20 | Feb 18–20 |
| Alberta | Family Day | Feb 20 | Feb 18–20 |
| Saskatchewan | Family Day | Feb 20 | Feb 18–20 |
| Manitoba | Family Day | Feb 20 | Feb 18–20 |
| New Brunswick | Family Day | Feb 20 | Feb 18–20 |
| Nova Scotia | Family Day | Feb 20 | Feb 18–20 |
| Prince Edward Island | Family Day | Feb 20 | Feb 18–20 |
| Newfoundland & Labrador | St. Patrick’s Day | Mar 17 | Mar 17–19 (if observed) |
| Quebec | Saint‑Jean‑Baptiste Day | Jun 24 | Jun 24–26 (if observed) |
| Ontario | Civic Holiday | Aug 7 | Aug 5–7 |
| British Columbia | Civic Holiday | Aug 7 | Aug 5–7 |
| Alberta | Civic Holiday | Aug 7 | Aug 5–7 |
| Saskatchewan | Civic Holiday | Aug 7 | Aug 5–7 |
| Manitoba | Civic Holiday | Aug 7 | Aug 5–7 |
| New Brunswick | Civic Holiday | Aug 7 | Aug 5–7 |
| Nova Scotia | Civic Holiday | Aug 7 | Aug 5–7 |
| Prince Edward Island | Civic Holiday | Aug 7 | Aug 5–7 |
| Newfoundland & Labrador | Civic Holiday | Aug 7 | Aug 5–7 |
| Quebec | Civic Holiday | Aug 7 | Aug 5–7 |

> **Tip:** For a fully accurate, province‑by‑province schedule, you can pull the official holiday calendars from each provincial government’s website or use a public API such as the *Canadian Holidays API* (e.g., https://date.nager.at/Api).  

Feel free to let me know if you’d like the data in a specific format (JSON, CSV, etc.) or if you need the provincial breakdown for a particular region. Happy planning!
